title: Not a leaf falls
hookLine: with Him are the keys of the unseen, and not a leaf falls without His knowing (6:59)
tomorrow: The stars, the moon, the sun, again

cards: A big tree lets go of more leaves in one autumn than anyone could count. Nobody tries; the groundskeeper with the leaf blower certainly doesn't.
Each one lets go at its own moment, twists on the way down, lands, and is gone under the next.
Of all the pictures the Qur'an could have picked to say Allah knows everything, verse fifty-nine of surah six reaches for that one. Not a mountain. Not a galaxy.

teach.b: The verse begins: with Him are the keys of the unseen, and no one knows them but He. The word for the unseen is ghayb: what is absent, hidden, out of sight; words from the same family describe someone who's away.
Belief in the ghayb is one of the first things the Qur'an says about the mindful, at the start of surah two: they believe in the unseen. Then the verse moves from the cosmic to the small.
He knows what is in the land and the sea. In Pickthall's words: “Not a leaf falleth but He knoweth it,” not a grain in the darkness of the earth, nothing wet or dry, but it's in a clear record.

A hadith in Bukhari says the keys of the unseen are five, and the Prophet ﷺ then recited the last verse of surah thirty-one: the knowledge of the Hour, the sending of rain, what is in the womb, what a person will earn tomorrow, and in what land a person will die.

teach.h: THE FIVE THAT NO ONE KNOWS.
teach.b: Things people long to know, and can't.
Muslim scholars cite this hadith to draw a line: no fortune-teller and no horoscope holds those keys. So the verse does two things at once. It humbles: you don't hold the keys.
And, in the verse's telling, it comforts: nothing goes unnoticed. Not the job you didn't get, not the hour you spent awake, not the small kindness no one saw.

teach.h: NOT A LEAF FALLETH BUT HE KNOWETH IT.

how: Belief in the ghayb, the unseen, is part of Muslim faith (2:3); scholars teach that its keys belong to Allah alone, which is why fortune-telling and horoscopes are widely discouraged.

games.q: a friend offers to read your future in the stars. according to 6:59 and the hadith of the five keys, who holds that knowledge?
games.why: with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. scholars use this verse to discourage fortune-telling.

practice: If you can see a tree or a plant, watch one leaf; if not, picture one, and follow it with your eyes as long as you can.
Then let your attention widen to all the other leaves, on all the other trees, in every city, right now, each one moving, with nobody you know watching them. Breathe with that.

wordCard.voice: Ghayb. The unseen: what is hidden from us, whose keys are with Allah alone, and not a leaf falls without His knowing. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the unseen, the hidden, what is absent from our senses.

carryVoice: Your line: not a leaf unknown. The small, unseen moments count too. I'm glad you came.
